newsitem.title: ITALY: Lower debt costs helping Italian accounts-Visco.
newsitem.headline: Lower debt costs helping Italian accounts-Visco.

text.p: Interest rates have fallen more rapidly than expected and are helping the government overhaul state accounts, Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco told parliament on Monday.
"The performance of (interest) rates has been much more comforting than expected," Visco told the lower house during a debate on the government's 1997 budget package.

"The final intervention needed to stabilise public finances will be much less thanks to the strong reduction in interest rates," he added. "The fall in rates represents an unprecedented reduction in spending."
Around 20 percent of government spending goes on servicing the country's mammoth debt mountain.

The yield on 10-year Italian bonds has fallen from around 11 percent in March to 8.1 percent at the start of November. Yields on short-term paper have also fallen sharply over the same period. The Bank of Italy's official discount rate has fallen 1.5 percentage points since March.
"Let us hope that in the future the central bank can follow market rates more closely. Approval of the budget would help this," Visco said.
The lower chamber is due to complete voting on the budget on November 14 after which the package passes to the Senate for further ratification.

He said a further fall in interest rates would stimulate the economy, Visco said, adding that there were "risks" gross domestic product (GDP) would not grow by 2.0 percent next year, as forecast by the government.
"It is possible this forecast will have to be looked at again...for good or bad," Visco said.
The Bank of Italy said last week it expected the economy would grow by around one percent in 1997.

"Growth would be helped by another autonomous, responsible decision to put the discount rate closer to market rates," Visco said. The discount rate currently stands at 7.50 percent. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
